title: Contravariant fibrations between right fibrations
statement: Use simplicial sets and universes from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], right fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and the contravariant model structure on $\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Fix a universe and let $S,X,Y$ be simplicial sets in it. Let $p:X\to S$ and $r:Y\to S$ be right fibrations, and let $u:X\to Y$ satisfy $ru=p$. Then $u$, regarded as a morphism of $\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$, is a fibration in the contravariant model structure if and only if the underlying simplicial map $u:X\to Y$ is a right fibration. No quasicategory or Kan hypothesis on $S$ is required.

source.place: HTT Corollary 2.2.3.14, printed pp. 86-87 (PDF pp. 104-105), used in the proof of GHN Proposition 9.7. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this contravariant-model theorem.

proof.text: Two model structures on the same category $\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$ occur: $M$, the contravariant model structure of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] named in the statement (weak equivalences by the mapping tests $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(-,Z)$), and $M'$, the cone-defined model structure of [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]. Both statements give the monomorphisms (degreewise injections) as cofibrations, and both say that the fibrant objects are exactly the right fibrations $X\to S$. Hence [lem-coef-model-structure-determined-by-fibrant-objects] gives that $M$ and $M'$ have the same weak equivalences, fibrations and trivial cofibrations. It therefore suffices to prove the assertion for $M'$. In Steps 2, 3, 6 and 7 below, model fibration, trivial cofibration, factorization and weak equivalence refer to $M'$, as stated in [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]; Step 5 uses [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] only for its separate statements about $\mathsf{RFib}(Y)$ and Kan mapping complexes.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.3.14, printed pp. 86–87; the homotopy-extension argument also used in Corollary 2.2.3.12.

proof.text: First prove the forward implication, also for later use with another domain. If $v:V\to Y$ is a contravariant model fibration over $S$, give any lifting square from a right horn $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<i\leq n$, to $v$ the structure map to $S$ obtained by composing its bottom map with $r$. The horn inclusion is right anodyne by [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne], hence a trivial cofibration over $S$ by [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]. The defining lifting property of a model fibration supplies the required filler. Thus $v$ lifts every right horn, which is exactly the right-fibration condition of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. In particular this proves the forward implication for $u$.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.3.14, printed pp. 86–87; the homotopy-extension argument also used in Corollary 2.2.3.12.

proof.text: For the converse assume that $u:X\to Y$ is a right fibration. In the model structure of [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model], factor $u$ as $X\xrightarrow{i}X'\xrightarrow{q}Y$ with $i$ a trivial cofibration and $q$ a fibration, all over $S$. Step 2 makes $q$ a right fibration. The composite $rq$ is a right fibration: in a horn problem first lift the projected upper horn through $r$, and then lift that resulting simplex through $q$, using [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Consequently $X,X',Y$ are right fibrations over $S$. The slice-model statement gives Kan complexes $X_s,X'_s,Y_s$ for every vertex $s$ of $S$, and, since $i$ is a model weak equivalence, it gives a weak homotopy equivalence $i_s:X_s\to X'_s$ for each such $s$.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.3.14, printed pp. 86–87; the homotopy-extension argument also used in Corollary 2.2.3.12.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S_0$. The restrictions $u_s:X_s\to Y_s$ and $q_s:X'_s\to Y_s$ are right fibrations: a right-horn square in either pullback is a square for $u$ or $q$, whose filler lies in the pullback because its composite to $S$ is the prescribed constant simplex at $s$. Since $Y_s$ is Kan, [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] makes both restrictions Kan fibrations. Apply [lem-coef-kan-fibration-arbitrary-base-fibers] to the map $i_s$ between these two Kan fibrations over the common base $Y_s$. It is a weak homotopy equivalence by Step 3, so every strict fiber map is a weak homotopy equivalence. For a vertex $y\in Y_s$, these strict fibers are exactly $X_y=X\times_Y\{y\}$ and $X'_y=X'\times_Y\{y\}$: specifying $u(x)=y$ already specifies $p(x)=r(y)=s$, degree by degree. Every vertex $y\in Y$ has such an $s=r(y)$, so $i_y:X_y\to X'_y$ is weak for every $y$.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.3.14, printed pp. 86–87; the homotopy-extension argument also used in Corollary 2.2.3.12.

proof.text: Regard $i$ as a map over $Y$ between the right fibrations $u$ and $q$. Step 4 and the fiberwise equivalence criterion of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], applied with base $Y$, give a simplicial homotopy inverse $g:X'\to X$ over $Y$ and a simplicial homotopy between $gi$ and $1_X$ over $Y$. We may take its orientation to be $h:X\times\Delta^1\to X$ with $h_0=1_X$ and $h_1=gi$. Indeed that same cited statement makes $\operatorname{Fun}_{/Y}(X,X)$ Kan. If the available edge is oriented $gi\to1_X$, fill the $2$-horn with vertices $(gi,1_X,gi)$, edge $01$ that edge and edge $02$ the identity at $gi$; the missing edge $12$ has the required reversed orientation. Thus $ug=q$ and $uh=u\operatorname{pr}_X$ hold strictly.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.3.14, printed pp. 86–87; the homotopy-extension argument also used in Corollary 2.2.3.12.

proof.text: To check the fibration lifting condition over $S$, let $j:A\hookrightarrow B$ be any trivial cofibration of that slice and let $a:A\to X$, $b:B\to Y$ satisfy $ua=bj$. Since $q$ is a model fibration, [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model] gives $e:B\to X'$ with $ej=ia$ and $qe=b$. Put $e'=ge$. Then $ue'=b$ and $e'j=gia$. On $A\times\Delta^1$ use $h(a\times1)$, and on $B\times\{1\}$ use $e'$. They agree on $A\times\{1\}$ because $h_1a=gia=e'j$. Their common composite to $Y$ is the restriction of $b\operatorname{pr}_B:B\times\Delta^1\to Y$. These formulas give a well-defined upper map from $(A\times\Delta^1)\cup_{A\times\{1\}}(B\times\{1\})$ to $X$.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.3.14, printed pp. 86–87; the homotopy-extension argument also used in Corollary 2.2.3.12.

proof.text: The inclusion of that union into $B\times\Delta^1$ is right anodyne. Specifically $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is the right horn $\Lambda_1^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$, hence is right anodyne by [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne], and $j$ is a monomorphism by [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]. Apply the pushout-product statement [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product] to this horn and $j$, interchanging the two factors of the degreewise products. By [lem-coef-right-anodyne-lifting-characterization], the right fibration $u$ lifts against this right anodyne map. Let $H:B\times\Delta^1\to X$ be a filler for the data of Step 6. Its endpoint $H_0$ satisfies $H_0j=a$ and $uH_0=b$, so solves the original lifting problem. This works for every trivial cofibration in the slice. The fibration characterization in [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model] proves that $u$ is a contravariant model fibration. All uses of Kan hypotheses concerned the strict vertex fibers, not $S$ or $Y$.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.3.14, printed pp. 86–87; the homotopy-extension argument also used in Corollary 2.2.3.12.

lean.statement: theorem contravariant_fibration_iff_rightFibration {S X Y : SSet.{u}} (D : SimplicialRightFibration.RightData S) (p : X ⟶ S) (r : Y ⟶ S) (f : X ⟶ Y) (comm : f ≫ r = p) (hp : rightFibration p) (hr : rightFibration r) : D.slice.simplicial.model.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations (Over.homMk f comm : Over.mk p ⟶ Over.mk r) ↔ rightFibration f
lean.note: The parameter D is the contravariant-model presentation data furnished by lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation (Presentation.right S). Its explicit fibration projection avoids any ambient Kan-model instance. The theorem works for every such presentation and uses the existing rightFibration predicate; no new definition or stronger base hypothesis is introduced.
